artifacts.summary: Five-phase plan adding a per-type removed<=added artifact-loss invariant as a FAIL-level --deep check in validate-state.sh, with an --allow-artifact-removal CLI opt-in, bidirectional fixture tests, an explicit append-only rule in rules/state-management.md, and a MUST NOT bullet on general-implementation-agent.

memory_candidates.content: In this agent system, specs/state.json's .artifacts array is append-only by INTENT but every sanctioned writer (skill_link_artifacts in skill-base.sh, orchestrator-postflight.sh Stage 8, link_artifact in reconcile-task-status.sh, skill-reviser SKILL.md Stage 8) implements a two-step 'remove-all-of-same-type, then add one' idiom -- the reference pattern taught in context/patterns/inline-status-update.md. Consequence for invariant design: a naive global path-superset rule ('every path present before must still be present') breaks every routine report/plan/summary re-link. The correct shape is a PER-TYPE COUNT invariant, removed(T) <= added(T), which is a no-op for first links (0/1), permits routine 1-for-1 supersession (1/1), and still rejects bulk loss (5 removed/2 added). Generalizable rule: before designing an append-only or monotonicity invariant over a shared data structure, empirically audit what the sanctioned writers actually do -- 'append-only by intent' rarely means literally append-only, and the gap between intent and behavior determines whether the invariant must be stated over sets or over per-partition counts.
